source_text: No, we don't want a special one off watcher.  We want a fully functional token-management system that works in the current live case.

reply_text:
㊥ (the token system) Understood, no watcher. I've designed a work-order (token) system for Agency, aimed at the codex-18/19/20 case, and two parts of it are being built now. Each delegated piece of work becomes a token that some agent always holds. When an agent's job ends while it still holds a token and nothing else is moving it, Agency nudges that agent once to either dispatch the next step or close the order. If that doesn't move it, Agency escalates. It runs on job ends, not a timer.

🈖 (how the stasis happens) codex-19 sends codex-20 work to implement and codex-18 work to replay, and each result comes back to codex-19 by auto-bellback. codex-19 then writes something like "handoff closed, codex-18 will replay", and its turn ends. If that turn dispatched nothing, all three sit idle, and nothing records that codex-19 still owes the next step. Right now codex-19 and codex-20 are both running, so it's moving at the moment.

㊢ (the design, `6819c30d` in E-agency-work-orders)
- **Open.** A work bell opens an order owed by the recipient, under the order the sender is working on. An agent's first work bell also opens a root order on the agent itself, owed to you. In this case that root is codex-19's mfuton chain.
- **Deliver.** When the recipient's job ends, the token goes back to the requester. When the requester's turn handling the result ends, the order closes.
- **Check.** The check runs when a job ends. If that agent owes an order, nothing below it is open, and it has no running job, queued job or park, it gets one nudge naming the order and the choice it owes. A second idle job end escalates to the requester, or to you for a root. After that it stops, so there's no reminder storm.
- **Kernel.** Each step is also written as a P24 act, so the kernel and the HUD read the same orders.

㊯ (two packets running, with parks)
- **W1, kimi-2:** the order ledger, open/deliver/close wired into Agency, and `GET /api/alpha/work-orders?agent=`. Job `invoke-…-7a3f8c08`, park `park-c140d67b-…`.
- **W2, kimi-3:** the pure stall check, tested on a fixture of this exact case: codex-19 idle after a delivered child gets a nudge, the second time it escalates to you. Job `invoke-…-f7cfdd97`, park `park-399f79e3-…`.

Both are running. Neither touches codex-18/19/20 or their jobs.

㊭ (then W3) When both are reviewed, W3 connects the check to job end and adds the close route and `agency_send.py --close-order`. From then on the system acts on the live case. Until W3 lands, `GET /api/alpha/work-orders?agent=codex-19` will show who holds each token, so you can see the stall without asking them for an update.

🈳 (one gap) codex-18 and codex-19 report to you through REPL turns, not bells, so "codex-18 will replay" doesn't open an order yet. The nudge still covers it, because codex-19 holds the root until it dispatches codex-18 or closes the root.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text:
(the excursion section) It records:
- **Your idea:** because 象 now reads after a turn lands, it can keep the marble-run state across turns.
- **The inputs that already exist:** 象's intents for your turns, the proforma marks in agent replies, and the commits in the "happened" note.
- **Tonight's open items** as a live example.
- **The missing adapter.**
- **That it's the same judge** as the reminders, shown to you instead of sent to an agent.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text:
(the adapter packet) One behaviour: a new pure namespace, `futon3c.xiang.turn-acts`, which turns a settled turn and the agent's marked reply into P24 acts. It comes with a function that gives `{:closed-this-turn … :still-open …}` for a turn. The packet also requires:
- **Act kinds** only from the kernel's own table; unknown intents are skipped and counted, never invented.
- **Act ids** stable, built from the record and fragment.
- **Links** between acts only where they're explicit, such as an accept after an offer, or a listed commit carrying an offer out.
- **The test fixture:** a few real turns from this session, copied read-only. It contains a 🈸 offer you accepted, which must close, and one you never answered, which must stay open.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text: (review) When it returns, I'll test the claim in the other direction too: remove your acceptance from the fixture, and the offer must then stay open. After that I'll propose the wiring and the HUD display as the next step.
